::: {.callout-warning}
## Status: stub, not yet drafted

This chapter is a placeholder. Real content to write here (drawing on
material already assembled across the project rather than starting from
nothing):

- Study area and setting: Steamboat Hills geothermal field, operated by
  Ormat Technologies, the Lower Sinter Terrace eruption context that
  motivates this thesis's spring-remapping fieldwork.
- Chloride discharge as a tracer of geothermal outflow -- Sorey's own
  framing [@sorey1992; @sorey2008; @sorey2017], extended in this project
  via continuous conductivity monitoring (SBRR/SBGG loggers) as a Cl
  proxy.
- The three stated thesis objectives (see `README.md`'s "Scientific
  Context and Purpose"): outflow characterization, Cl-conductivity
  calibration, and potentiometric/transport mapping.
- What has changed since Sorey & Colvard (1992) [@sorey1992] and Sorey
  (2000) [@sorey2000] -- both document a spring-flow cessation that had,
  as of 2000, not reversed even after the groundwater-level driver
  partly blamed for it did reverse; whether this remains true in 2026 is
  a live, testable question this thesis's own fieldwork can answer.
:::
